name: Global Preference Survey: risk, patience, reciprocity, altruism and trust
author: Human Not Found
description: Original study: Falk, A., Becker, A., Dohmen, T., Enke, B., Huffman, D., & Sunde, U. (2018). Global evidence on economic preferences. The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 133(4), 1645-1692. The Global Preference Survey measured risk taking, patience, positive and negative reciprocity, altruism and trust among 80,000 people in representative samples of 76 countries, with survey items validated against incentivized experiments. Preferences varied strongly between countries and even more within them, and predicted saving, schooling, health and prosocial behaviour. This template asks ten participants of mixed age, gender and occupation the survey's qualitative items, with six conditions placing them in the United States, Germany, Sweden, Japan, Nigeria or Brazil. The original's quantitative staircase items (lottery and time-delay choices) are left out, so the composite preference indices cannot be rebuilt exactly; compare item means across countries with the country-level data published by the authors. Participants are simulated: each is a Model participant, using the free test model until you choose a model, so the first runs only check the design; with the test model every participant takes the sample answer.

items.prompt: In general, how willing or unwilling are you to take risks? 0 = completely unwilling, 10 = very willing.
How willing are you to give up something that is beneficial for you today in order to benefit more from that in the future? 0 = completely unwilling, 10 = very willing.
When someone does me a favor I am willing to return it. 0 = does not describe me at all, 10 = describes me perfectly.
If I am treated very unjustly, I will take revenge at the first occasion, even if there is a cost to do so. 0 = does not describe me at all, 10 = describes me perfectly.
How willing are you to punish someone who treats you unfairly, even if there may be costs for you? 0 = completely unwilling, 10 = very willing.
How willing are you to punish someone who treats others unfairly, even if there may be costs for you? 0 = completely unwilling, 10 = very willing.
How willing are you to give to good causes without expecting anything in return? 0 = completely unwilling, 10 = very willing.
Imagine that today you unexpectedly received an amount equal to about 1,000 euro in your local currency. How much of it, in euro, would you donate to a good cause? (0 to 1000)
I assume that people have only the best intentions. 0 = does not describe me at all, 10 = describes me perfectly.
